spec.effect: ICE trail, or "rime fuse": a frost lace of six-fold stellar crystals is laid along the path as kitty's leading corners pass. It holds with one soft glint moving tail to head. It then sublimates tail first, shedding hexagonal platelets (diamond dust) that drift down. It is drawn only in the cursor's colour, with intensity as opacity. The design targets the uncommitted `baud-render/src/effect.rs` framework (Effect enum, EffectU = 24-float prefix + k[8], Kind::Band/Kind::Particle), which is in the working tree now. It departs from the contract in two places, and both are open questions (see open_questions 1 and 2): its bands cover the path capsule, not only the emitter quad, and optional shard rotation needs a vertex branch. Prototype: scratchpad/trail/new/ice/proto/ice.swift. Contact sheets: scratchpad/trail/new/ice/ice-{hop,diag}-{dark,light}.png, at ages 30/80/150/250/350/450/550/650/800 ms.

prior_art.name: Neovide cursor_vfx.rs: pixiedust, sonicboom, ripple, railgun, torpedo
prior_art.what_to_take: Pixiedust (lines 341-346, 417-429) is the closest existing effect in the cursor's colour. It sheds particles along the travel, drawn as squares in the cursor's background colour at an alpha that falls with remaining life. Its launch direction biases toward +y, which is down in pixel coordinates, and its lifetime is scaled by position along the path. The shards take three things from it: shed along the path, drift down, fade by life. They are closed form rather than Neovide's integrated update. Sonicboom and ripple only confirm that effects stay in the cursor's colour.

prior_art.name: A. Riccardi, FreezePostProcess.shader (Unity, 2019)
prior_art.what_to_take: Frost progression as a threshold on a static field, driven by one animated amount: gradient = pow(opacity, steepness - amount*steepness) * amount (line 102). That is closed-form freezing with no simulation state, and it is the principle here: each crystal's growth and melt are functions of age against a per-seed deposit time. Riccardi's field is a texture; this design's is procedural, and uses no texture reads.

prior_art.name: Stefan Gustavson, webgl-noise cellular2D / cellular2x2 (Worley noise on GPU)
prior_art.what_to_take: Two ideas, weighed and rejected. A jitter below 1 gives a more regular, hexagonal cell pattern. The 2x2 search is cheaper but has artefacts. Either way a grain sheet costs a 9-to-16-cell search per pixel. The 1-D seed lattice along the path needs 3 seeds per pixel, proven complete.

prior_art.name: K. G. Libbrecht, 'Snow Crystals' (arXiv 1910.06389v2, 2019)
prior_art.licence: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence 1.0; facts only
prior_art.what_to_take: The physics the crystal shape follows. PDF p.414: 'Sidebranches typically form at 60-degree angles relative to their primary branches.' p.52: 'All six a-axes point to corners of the hexagonal prism.' p.22: six branches sprout from a hexagonal plate's corners by a branching instability. So: arms on the six corners, side branches at 60 degrees, a plate at the centre, with no hue involved.

prior_art.name: cabbibo/snowflake: ss-snowflake.glsl, ss-diffusion.glsl, fs-hex.glsl
prior_art.licence: NO LICENCE (all rights reserved), read only
prior_art.what_to_take: Negative evidence. Real crystal growth on the GPU is a ping-pong simulation over textures (t_pos/t_oPos/t_og), the Reiter-style cellular model. That is state between frames, which contract rule 2 forbids. It is why growth here is a closed-form ease over a fixed shape, not a simulation.

spec.look:
Frame by frame, for a 30-column hop or a long diagonal, with the chosen defaults: light cursor on a dark ground, or dark on light through the same premultiplied rule. Per-frame renders are in the contact sheets.

- 0-40 ms: kitty's quad slides from the old cursor to the new one as a faint pane of ice: a 14% body with a crisp 1-px rim at 50%. Just behind its leading edge, small six-armed crystals nucleate along the path and grow outward. Around them a patchy frosted haze, the rime (up to 24%), fills a band about a cell tall. The frost front tracks the quad's leading corners, because deposition uses kitty's own fast constant.
- 40-150 ms: the pane fades out by 0.15 s. What is left is a lace of snow crystals scattered about a cell above and below the path, varying about 2x in size. Each has six thin arms (95%, tapering), short side branches at 60 degrees (60%) and a translucent hexagonal centre plate (30%). The inner side branches of neighbouring arms meet on the 30-degree mirror and form chevrons and hex rings, the sectored-plate look.
- 100-250 ms: hold. One soft glint, a 1.4-unit-wide band, travels tail to head and lifts the lines by up to 30%. It reads as light catching ice.
- From 250 ms, sublimation, tail first: each crystal shrinks toward its centre (arms to 35%) and fades over 0.22 s. The melt front walks from tail to head over 0.2 s. As each stretch sublimates it sheds hexagonal platelets, 8-15 px across, that pop up slightly and then drift down, fading. The crystals at the cursor are gone by 0.70 s, the last platelet by at most 0.87 s.
- The cursor's own rectangle is never covered. On the light theme the same frames are dark lace on light (see ice-*-light.png).
spec.design:
Units: c = unit = cell height in px (whole pixels: baud's cell_h is a Px). All frost maths is relative to the tail:
- rel = (p - tail) / c
- D = dir, Pp = (-D.y, D.x), Lu = len / c
- along = dot(rel, D), across = dot(rel, Pp)
- d_seg = |rel - D * clamp(along, 0, Lu)|, the capsule distance
- d_q = fx_distance(p) / c, the quad distance

REJECT: a pixel in the hole draws nothing. If d_seg > reach and d_q > reach, draw nothing.

PANE, kitty's quad:
- pa = sat(1 - age / (0.6 * HOLD)), which fades by 0.15 s
- pane = pa * max(0.14 * (1 - smoothstep(-0.5, 0.5, dq_px)), 0.5 * (1 - smoothstep(0.5, 1.5, |dq_px|)))

If d_seg > reach, return pane.

LINE: W = max(k_width, 0.75 / c) and aa = 0.5 / c. line(d, w) = 1 - smoothstep(w - aa, w + aa, d).

SEEDS, a 1-D lattice along the path, with no count needed:
- k0 = floor(along / S + 0.5); evaluate k in {k0-1, k0, k0+1}; frost = max over the three.
- sbase = fx_hash(seed + 0x1CE01CE0)
- h1 = fx_hash(uint(int(k)) + sbase), then h2..h6 = fx_hash of the previous. k may be -1: bit-cast it, never clamp.
- along_k = (k + (unit(h1) - 0.5) * 0.5) * S. The along jitter J = S/4.
- across_k = (unit(h2) - 0.5) * 0.7
- win = smoothstep(-0.25, 0, along_k) * (1 - smoothstep(Lu, Lu + 0.25, along_k)). This smooth window replaces a seed count, so a rounding difference moves opacity by an ULP, not by a whole crystal.
- u_k = sat(along_k / Lu); delay = 0.03 * unit(h5)

TIMING, per crystal:
- Deposit time is kitty's leading-corner closed form inverted: t_dep(u) = -LEAD * log2(max(1 - 0.999 u, 1e-3)), with LEAD = TAU_FAST / 10 = 0.01 s. This matches the quad's leading edge; a linear 0.10 s front would lag it.
- x = sat((age - t_dep(u_k) - delay) / GROW); grow = 1 - (1 - x)^3
- m = HOLD + SPREAD * u_k + delay; fade = 1 - smoothstep(m, m + MELT, age)
- L = ARM * (0.45 + 0.55 unit(h4)) * grow * (0.35 + 0.65 fade)
- exist = sat(L / (2W))

CRYSTAL SHAPE:
- r = rel - (D * along_k + Pp * across_k)
- Rotation by a hashed angle in [0, 60) degrees, with no trig. s = 0.57735027 * unit(h3), cs = (1 - s^2) / (1 + s^2), sn = 2s / (1 + s^2). w = (cs r.x + sn r.y, -sn r.x + cs r.y).
- D6 fold into the wedge [0, 30] degrees, arm on +x:
  - w = abs(w)
  - w -= 2 max(dot(w, nA), 0) nA, with nA = (-0.8660254, 0.5), the 60-degree mirror
  - w -= 2 max(dot(w, nB), 0) nB, with nB = (-0.5, 0.8660254), the 30-degree mirror
- Main arm: dm = |w - (clamp(w.x, 0, L), 0)|; Wm = W (1.4 - 0.7 sat(w.x / max(L, 1e-4))); mainA = 0.95 line(dm, Wm).
- Side branch, at 60 degrees, e = (0.5, 0.8660254):
  - xr = w.x - w.y * 0.57735027
  - j = max(floor(xr / B + 0.5), 1); xj = j B
  - lj = min(0.6 (L - xj), xj). Capped at xj, the branch stops on the 30-degree mirror, where it meets its mirror image and forms a hex ring.
  - v = w - (xj, 0); h = clamp(dot(v, e), 0, max(lj, 0)); ds = |v - h e|
  - sideA = 0.60 line(ds, W) sat(lj / (2W))
- Centre plate: pr = 0.10 + 0.30 unit(h6)^2; dp = dot(w, (0.8660254, 0.5)) - pr L 0.8660254; plateA = 0.30 (1 - smoothstep(-aa, aa, dp)).
- crystal = max(mainA, sideA, plateA) * exist * fade * win

GLINT:
- gp = (age - 0.4 HOLD) / (0.6 HOLD) * (Lu + 2S) - S
- gl = 1 - smoothstep(0, S, |along - gp|)
- frost = sat(frost * (1 + 0.3 gl))

RIME, which reuses fire's fx_noise:
- u = sat(along / Lu); front = (Lu + 0.6)(1 - exp2(-age / LEAD)) - 0.3
- dep = 1 - smoothstep(front - 0.3, front + 0.3, along)
- rfade = 1 - smoothstep(HOLD + SPREAD u, HOLD + SPREAD u + MELT, age)
- s2 = seed ^ 0x51ED0000; q2 = (0.8 rel.x - 0.6 rel.y, 0.6 rel.x + 0.8 rel.y)
- n = 0.65 fx_noise(rel * 2.3, s2) + 0.35 fx_noise(q2 * 6.7, s2 + 0x9E3779B9)
- rime = 0.24 (1 - smoothstep(0.15, 0.6, d_seg)) smoothstep(0.35, 0.75, n) dep rfade

OUTPUT: a = color.a * max(frost, rime, pane), drawn as (color.rgb * a, a).

PARAMS (k[8], owned by Rust):
- S = SPACING 0.70 u, ARM 0.62 u, k_width 0.028 u
- B = BRANCH 0.21 u
- GROW 0.12 s, HOLD 0.25 s, SPREAD 0.20 s, MELT 0.22 s

REACH is 1.15 u around the segment. Analytic bound: a crystal centre is at most sqrt(0.25^2 + 0.35^2) = 0.43 u from the segment, plus arm 0.62 u, plus 1.4W + aa = 0.054 u, which is 1.105 u. Measured worst min(d_seg, d_q) at a lit pixel: 0.881 u over 1.92 M random samples plus the retarget trials. Rime reaches 0.6 u; the pane lies within 1.5 px of the quad.

LIFE, the body: HOLD + SPREAD + MELT + 0.03 = 0.70 s. The last crystal fades by then.

END: max(LIFE, last shard death), in [0.70, 0.866] s. The latest live shard over 200 seeds was at 0.858 s.

SUPPORT (framework change 1, open question 1): one band record per cell row. Its x-interval is the hull of the capsule's interval (corners [tail, head, head, tail]) and the emitter quad's interval, each widened by reach * unit. It uses fire's clipping loop over two polygons.
- The hull is needed, not the capsule alone. A long move within REIGNITE keeps the old path and sends the quad elsewhere. A short move snaps the emitter to wherever the cursor is.
- Prototype with the retarget case: 0 lit pixels missed and 0 doubled, of 118,612.
- Cost lever: clip the capsule tail to along = Lu * sat((age - HOLD - MELT) / SPREAD), which is where everything is melted, and the head to along = Lu * min(1, (1 - exp2(-age / LEAD)) / 0.999) + 0.3, the deposition front. The bands grow to the head in about 0.1 s and after that only shrink.
- Fire keeps support = emitter, so its records do not change.

WCAG 2.3.1: one appear-and-disappear pair per ignition; see photosensitivity.

DRIVER: Style::Effect(Effect::Ice), unchanged. It lights on moves over 2 cells; a move within REIGNITE = 334 ms retargets the quad and keeps the burning ignition; a snap or a hidden cursor puts it out. The CPU path runs it as the quad (chase_style), as it does fire. Config: `trail = "ice"`.
spec.particles:
Diamond-dust shards: hexagonal platelets shed as the lace sublimates. Each is a closed-form function of the seed and the age, one Kind::Particle record.

- Count: n = clamp(round(Lu * 1.5), 8, 96).
- Hashes: shard i takes h0 = fx_hash(seed ^ (i * 0x9E3779B9) ^ 0x5AAD5AAD), then h1..h5 in a chain.
- Birth and life: along = unit(h0); born = HOLD + SPREAD * along + 0.3 * MELT * unit(h5); life = 0.20 + 0.15 unit(h1). a = age - born; the shard is alive when 0 <= a <= life.
- p0 = tail + D * len * along + Pp * ((unit(h2) - 0.5) * 0.7 c)
- v0 = ((unit(h3) - 0.5) * 1.2 c, -(0.2 + 0.6 unit(h4)) c), a small upward pop as it breaks off
- Drag K = 3/s and gravity G = 6 c/s^2, downward, so the terminal velocity is 2 cells/s:
  - s = (1 - e^(-K a)) / K
  - centre = (p0.x + v0.x s + 0.10 c sin(9a + phase), p0.y + v0.y s + (G c / K)(a - s))
  - phase = 2 pi unit(h1 ^ 0x5bd1e995)
- heat = 1 - a / life; radius = c (0.12 + 0.10 unit(h2)) (0.6 + 0.4 heat); glow = 0.9 heat. The record colour is fill at glow.
- The record is the existing ember record: side = max(ceil(2 radius), 2), centred.

FRAGMENT (ice_fragment, KIND_PARTICLE):
- d = sdHexagon(uv, 0.70), iq's MIT form: p = abs(p); p -= 2 min(dot(k, p), 0) k with k = (-0.866025404, 0.5); p -= (clamp(p.x, -0.577350269 r, 0.577350269 r), r); d = |p| sign(p.y).
- a = in.color.a * (1 - smoothstep(-0.08, 0.12, d)) * (0.55 + 0.45 smoothstep(-0.35, -0.02, d)): a plate with a brighter rim.
- The vertex count 0.70 / cos 30 + 0.12 = 0.93 < 1, so the plate fits the record under any turn.

DEFAULT: unrotated, flat-top, which fits contract rule 3 with no vertex change.

OPTION, open question 3: in-plane spin. theta = (pi/3) unit(h5) + (unit(h4) - 0.5) * 8 a, computed in Rust with sin/cos. The encoding is chosen so (0, 0) means identity: u = round((1 - cos theta) * 32767.5) and v = (round(sin theta * 32767) as i16) as u16. Fire's embers, at turn (1, 0), therefore keep u = v = 0 and their records are unchanged. The shader side is in the MSL sketch.

uniform_params.name: k[0] SPACING
uniform_params.meaning: Seed lattice pitch along the path. Seed k sits at (k + (unit(h1) - 0.5) * 0.5) * S. With the along jitter J = S/4, three neighbours are complete while (ARM + 1.4W + aa + J)/S + 0.5 < 2; here 1.71.

uniform_params.name: k[1] ARM
uniform_params.meaning: Largest arm length. A crystal's arm is ARM * (0.45 + 0.55 unit(h4)) at full growth.

uniform_params.name: k[2] WIDTH
uniform_params.meaning: Branch line half-width. The shader floors it at 0.75 px (max(k2, 0.75/c)); the main arm tapers from 1.4x to 0.7x.

uniform_params.name: k[3] BRANCH
uniform_params.meaning: Spacing of the side-branch roots along an arm. Branches leave at 60 degrees, length min(0.6 (L - x_j), x_j).

uniform_params.name: k[4] GROW
uniform_params.meaning: Time from deposit to full size, eased 1 - (1 - x)^3. No transcendental functions.

uniform_params.name: k[5] HOLD
uniform_params.meaning: When the tail starts to melt. It also times the glint (0.4-1.0 HOLD) and the pane's fade (0.6 HOLD).

uniform_params.name: k[6] SPREAD
uniform_params.meaning: How long the melt front takes from tail to head: m(u) = HOLD + SPREAD u.

uniform_params.name: k[7] MELT
uniform_params.meaning: Each crystal's and the rime's fade duration; arms shrink to 35% while fading.

uniform_params.name: prefix life
uniform_params.meaning: The body's life. The shader does not read it for ice; Effect::life and the band clipping do.

uniform_params.name: prefix reach
uniform_params.meaning: Distance around the path segment (and the emitter quad) beyond which ice_frost returns 0. Analytic bound 1.105; measured worst 0.881.

uniform_params.name: shader literal ICE_LEAD
uniform_params.meaning: Kitty's leading-corner constant. The deposit time t_dep(u) = -LEAD log2(1 - 0.999u) and the rime front 1 - exp2(-age/LEAD) follow the quad's leading edge. A literal, because k[8] is full; pinned to the Rust constant by a new test in the SHAPE_SLOTS style.

uniform_params.name: shader literals ICE_SALT / RIME_SALT
uniform_params.meaning: Hash salts that separate the crystal and rime streams from fire's, drawn from the same seed. Spelled once in Rust and once in MSL, and pinned by a test like the kind codes.

spec.life_seconds: Body LIFE is 0.70 s: HOLD 0.25 + SPREAD 0.20 + MELT 0.22 + a 0.03 hash delay; the last crystal, at the head, is gone by then. END = max(LIFE, last shard death), in [0.70, 0.866] s. A shard is born at HOLD + SPREAD*along + 0.3*MELT*h and lives 0.20-0.35 s. The prototype's latest live shard over 200 seeds was at 0.858 s. Fire's end is 0.45-0.85 s.
spec.photosensitivity:
WCAG 2.3.1: at most three general flashes a second.

- Each ignition is one appear and one disappear, a single pair spread over about 0.7 s: growth 0.12 s, melt 0.22 s per crystal, staggered 0.2 s tail to head. The driver's REIGNITE (334 ms) caps ignitions at three a second, so the frost's pairs stay at three or fewer a second.
- Nothing inside an ignition flickers. There is no time-varying noise: the rime noise is static in space; only its fade moves.
- Nothing inside an ignition oscillates. There is no breathing or hue cycling.
- The glint is the one extra rise-and-fall. It is local by construction: at most 2*SPACING = 1.4 cells along the path, times the frost band, at most 2.3 cells across. That is about 3.2 cell^2, roughly 3,700 device px^2 at 34-px cells, or about 930 CSS px^2 at 2x. The WCAG area threshold is about 21,800 px^2, 25% of a 10-degree field at 1024x768. The glint also raises line opacity by only 30%.
- Shards fade monotonically.
- A full-screen diagonal's frost band can exceed the area threshold as a whole. It still flashes only once per ignition, so the REIGNITE cap is what keeps it compliant. That cap must stay.
spec.rust_reference_notes:
What the pixel oracle's reference, `ice_reference` beside `fire_reference` in baud-present-macos/tests/cells.rs, must port. proto/ice.swift is a line-for-line f32 spelling of it: sha256 1eb72d416347818a1a4bb8c637d29d8a91c5611e19735bb4c85d75df361c3922, functions crystal, iceAlpha, shards, shardAlpha, bands.

1. Reuse fire's third spelling of fx_hash / fx_unit / fx_lattice / fx_noise (the `Word` type) and of fx_distance. Nothing new in the noise.
2. Discrete steps, spelled identically in both languages:
   - k0 = floor(along/S + 0.5) and j = floor(xr/B + 0.5). Not round() or rint().
   - A seed index is hashed as uint(int(k)) in MSL and (k as i32).cast_unsigned() in Rust. k0 - 1 is -1 at the tail: bit-cast it, never clamp it.
   - Rotation uses the tan(half-angle) rational form, and the fold uses two reflections: no atan, sin or cos anywhere in the frost.
3. A k0 flip is harmless. At a rounding boundary the GPU and Rust may pick neighbouring k0. The seed that leaves the {k0-1..k0+1} window is then 1.5S - J = 0.875 cells away, beyond the 0.675 cells a crystal reaches (ARM + 1.4W + aa). The prototype's brute-force check does not exercise this; the bound covers it.
4. Transcendentals in the shader: only log2 in the deposit time, exp2 in the rime front, and sqrt in length(). All feed smoothsteps, so fast-math ULP errors stay under one step of 255. No precise:: math is needed. Expect fire's tolerance: one step of 255, 20 pixels a scene.
5. Records: the reference composites the renderer's own records, as fire's does:
   - bands (Kind::Band, fill opaque), each pixel at its centre in the record's integer rect;
   - particles (Kind::Particle), with uv = 2*(p - rec.xy)/rec.wh - 1 on the integer rect.
   - If rotation is taken, uv is rotated by the quantised turn, decoded as cs = 1 - u/32767.5 and sn = (v as i16)/32767 -- never the exact cos/sin.
   - The shard glow reaches the fragment through the record's alpha Chan::from_unit(glow), quantised; use the record's colour, not the float.
6. Two unit tests the oracle cannot replace, because both arms and the reference use the same records:
   - Every lit pixel lies in exactly one band. Prototype: 0 missed and 0 doubled over the retarget, hop and diagonal cases (118,612 + 69,783 lit pixels).
   - Ice bands respect the reach, for which fire's every_pixel_within_reach_is_in_a_band is the template.
7. A latent fire issue the same test found. The shared band builder takes top = floor(band) and bottom = ceil(band + unit), so a fractional unit double-covers a pixel row: 1,473 doubled pixels at unit 33.5. That double-blends. It is latent only because cell_h is a whole-pixel Px; a unit test should pin that precondition.
8. Framework changes, each leaving fire's pixels unchanged:
   (a) Effect::support. Fire returns the emitter corners; ice returns the capsule plus the quad, merged per row into one hull interval. Gate: the existing oracle scenes plus fire's band test, byte-identical records.
   (b) Particle.turn, only if rotation is taken, encoded so (0, 0) is identity. Fire embers keep u = v = 0. Gate: fire's the_records_are_the_cursors_colour test plus the oracle.
   (c) ICE_LEAD and the two salts as pinned shader literals. Gate: a new pin test.

spec.cost_vs_fire:
Nothing here is measured on the GPU; these are counts.

Per pixel inside the reach:
- Fire: a 4-octave fbm (16 lattice samples, 32 PCG hashes) plus 2 quad-distance loops (8 lengths).
- Ice: 1 quad-distance loop (4 lengths), 1 capsule distance, 3 crystals (6 hashes, 2 divides and 3 lengths each, with early-outs for crystals not yet deposited or already melted), and a 2-octave rime (8 lattice samples, 16 hashes).
- Totals: about 35 hashes and 14 lengths for ice, against fire's 32 and about 8. Roughly equal ALU, and no texture reads.

Covered area is where ice costs more:
- Fire's bands follow the collapsing quad.
- Ice's cover the path capsule, 2.3 cells wide, until HOLD + MELT = 0.47 s. After that the capsule tail is clipped behind the melt front, and the head is clipped to the deposition front. So they grow to the head in about 0.1 s and then only shrink, gone by 0.70 s.
- Kitty's trailing corners take 0.36-0.46 s, so during the first ~0.4 s the two cover a similar area. Ice holds the whole path about 0.1 s longer, then sheds it.
- A full-screen diagonal therefore costs more than fire's for 0.25-0.5 s.

Particles: at most 96 shards against fire's 160 embers, each a few-pixel record with one hexagon SDF.

Frames: the same 120 Hz frame count while alive, like fire. Life is up to 0.87 s against fire's 0.45-0.85, so under typing expect somewhat more than fire's measured +0.68% of a core per newline trail (see open questions).
risks: The contract's rule 4 says bands go over the reach around the emitter quad; ice needs the path capsule too. The alternative that fits rule 4 exactly is frost only while kitty's quad covers a point. Measured from Segment::at for a 30-column hop, a path point is inside the quad only from 1.5-7 ms (u=0.1), 10-41 ms (u=0.5) and 31-143 ms (u=0.9). That is a 30-110 ms flicker along the path, shorter than GROW 0.12 s, so no lace could form. The capsule support is what makes the look possible, and it is a design decision, not an implementation detail.

The design is built against the uncommitted effect.rs refactor in the working tree (EffectU with k[8], Kind::Band/Particle, fx_* names). If that refactor changes shape -- the prefix, PARAMS = 8, how particles are drawn -- the uniform layout and the support hook here move with it.

The shared band builder double-covers a pixel row when unit is fractional (prototype: 1,473 doubled pixels at unit 33.5). Fire has the same code and is safe only because cell_h is a whole-pixel Px. It needs a pinned precondition or top/bottom made disjoint.

Visual literalness: the frames read as a garland of snowflakes at 34-px cells. At 1x (17-px cells) the 0.75-px line floor makes the branches a faint blur; only the arms and plates read. The renders are all at 34 px, so the 1x look is not rendered and unverified.
The dark-on-light theme shows dark lace. The renders read as frost or engraving, but it may read as ink or soot.
Life up to 0.87 s is longer than fire's; every newline's trail keeps frames alive longer. That costs CPU per Metal submission (~0.24 ms a frame), not GPU.

The prototype checks the formulas on the CPU only. The fast-math tolerance (one step of 255) is assumed from fire's measured behaviour, not measured for this shader. Precision of log2, exp2 and division in MSL fast math against Rust is expected at ULP level but unproven until the oracle runs.
Diamond-dust shards are small (8-15 px) and unrotated by default. Without spin they may read as static hexagon dots; rotation needs the vertex branch (open question 3).
open_questions: Rule 4 (bands around the emitter quad) versus laid frost. Should ice's bands cover the path capsule (tail to head, 1.15 cells) as well as kitty's quad, so the lace can form and hold? The alternative that keeps rule 4 exactly: frost appears only while the quad covers a point. Measured, that is 10-41 ms at mid-path and 31-143 ms near the head, too short for crystals to grow (0.12 s); it reads as a brief shimmer, not frost.

Shards: plain unrotated hexagonal platelets with no vertex-shader change (fits rule 3; the default here), or slowly spinning ones? Spinning needs Particle.turn plus a four-line branch in glyph_vertex, encoded so fire's embers are unchanged.

Light theme: frost there is dark lace (the cursor's dark colour at the same opacities). Is that acceptable, or should line opacity be capped lower on light themes? A cap would be a theme-dependent number, which the fire trail does not have. See ice-hop-light.png and ice-diag-light.png.

Life: up to 0.87 s (hold 0.25 s, melt spread 0.20 s, melt 0.22 s), longer than fire's 0.45-0.85 s. Fire already costs +0.68% of a core under typing because its life is time-bound. Shorten HOLD, or let a keystroke hasten the melt? The latter changes the look.

Density and literalness: the current constants give a visible garland of stellar crystals (spacing 0.7 cells, arms up to 0.62 cells). Keep that, or thin it toward a sparser, more abstract rime -- fewer crystals, more haze? This is a taste call the contact sheets are for.
